newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says aims stake in TV station.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says aims stake in TV station.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd is considering to take up a stake in a television broadcasting company, its chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said on Wednesday.
The national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying that the TV company targeted could be a local or foreign one.

Telekom has also not decided on which company it would buy, he told reporters when asked to comment on market speculation the telecommunications giant is eyeing a 20 percent stake in local private station, Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Bhd, or TV3.
He said at a company function that it was important for companies like Telekom to be involved in the entertainment and information industries.

The Star newspaper reported on Tuesday that diversified Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd, which has a 43.2 percent stake in TV3, plans to sell the station to Telekom at about 6.0 ringgit a share, or a total of 200 million ringgit.
TV3 stock ended at 5.75 ringgit at the end of Wednesday trading.
